items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to adjudications and
owner liability for a violation of traffic-control signal indications in the
county of Westchester; to amend the public officers law, in relation to
accessing records; and providing for the repeal of certain provisions upon
expiration thereof
items.lawCode: Amd §1803, add §1111-g, V & T L; amd §87, Pub Off L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7026

SPONSOR: STEWART-COUSINS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to adjudi-
cations and owner liability for a violation of traffic-control signal
indications in the county of Westchester; to amend the public officers
law, in relation to accessing records; and providing for the repeal of
certain provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to prevent reckless driving and reduce the
number of accidents while making the streets of Westchester County safer
for drivers and pedestrians.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds a new section to the Vehicle and traffic law authorizing
Westchester County to adopt local laws establishing a red-light camera
program within the county, consisting of cameras at no more than fifty
intersections that only photograph the license plate of a vehicle and
not the driver, the passengers, or the contents of the vehicle. It also
establishes that the owner of a vehicle is liable for any red-light
camera violation caused by any permitted driver of the vehicle. Addi-
tionally, it establishes a $50 maximum fine for each violation, with an
additional $25 penalty permitted for a failure to respond to a notice of
liability within the allotted time, and that Westchester County must
send notice of such violation by first class mail to each registered
owner of the vehicle.

Section 2 adds a new subsection to the existing Vehicle and Traffic Law
Section 1803 stating that the court, judge, or officer who collects the
fine for the red-light camera violation must send the money to the State
Comptroller within the first 10 days of the month following collection,
and the Comptroller will divide the fine with 80% going to Westchester
County and 20% going to the general fund of the town or village where
the traffic light was run.

Section 3 amends Section 87(2) of the Public Officers by adding para-
graph (t), establishing that agencies may deny access to, and separate
from public inspection and copying, any "photographs, microphotographs,
videotape, or other recorded images" created in relation to red-light
camera laws.

Section 4 states that the purchasing or leasing of equipment for the
demonstration program established in this bill shall be subject to the
same rules regarding advertisements for bids and offers, found in

Section 103 of the General Municipal Law as other public projects.

Section 5 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Westchester County police have witnessed an uptick in drivers moving
through red lights. The Red Light Camera program has shown effectiveness
in other jurisdictions in reducing such incidents and promoting greater
public safety. Westchester seeks the State's permission to implement a
system at the traffic signals with the highest accident rates in order
to dissuade drivers of unsafe driving habits.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S6493A Stewart-Cousins - Passed Senate, Reported and Commit-
ted to Rules

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall expire and be deemed repealed on December 1,
2027, provided, further, that any such local law as may be enacted
pursuant to section one of this act shall remain in full force and
effect only until December 1, 2027.
